page.description: CentOS Stream editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: The continuous stream that RHEL is built from: one rolling major version, rebuilt nightly. Boot image or full DVD, then write it to a stick.
pros: Sits directly upstream of RHEL, so fixes land here first.
A rolling major version instead of point releases to migrate between.
Boot, DVD and cloud images from the same build.
The build date is printed in every file name.
cons: Not a stable-release distribution; packages move.
No end-of-life date for a stream; it rolls forward.
Fewer third-party repositories target Stream than RHEL.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was available, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was available for CentOS Stream; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: One path per image: boot or DVD, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk. The pinned build is dated 2026-10-26.
